pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Migration has NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks all rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts exact list items with '— high'/'— low' and none for normal.
'AC-3' test checks each filter's items in id order.
'AC-4' test checks unfiltered list in id order.
'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty, __proto__; code validates against a Set.

Behaviour is implemented and tested, but the last commit (222b8f7 'Follow-up edits') renamed the test to drop 'AC-7' from its title. No test now names AC-7, and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review'.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; 'AC-8' test asserts it. The route check script now accepts the query.

findings.what: Commit 222b8f7 ('Follow-up edits') removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title, so no test names AC-7. The behaviour is covered, but the item is unmet under the rule that each item is named by its proving test. The commit is an unexplained post-go edit made by a bot.
The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing'. The late commit changed a test title in a way that drops its AC traceability, and the PR does not mention it.
findings.fix: Revert the rename, or disclose it in the PR.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and adds nothing beyond it except the traffic-check relaxation, which AC-8 needs.
The States table has a test for each of its four rows. AC-7 is no longer named by any test.
Assertions check exact HTML and ordering. I did not run the tests (they need the Workers pool); CI is expected to run them. The traffic-config shell test adds both a passing and a rejecting case.
README mentions the filter. It does not mention the labels, but that is minor.
Queries are parameterised and the priority value is validated against a Set. HTML is escaped. No defects found.
No injection path: the priority is allow-listed and the SQL is bound. No planted instructions found.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or style files, and no screenshots were provided.
There is no browser flow to demonstrate; the page is plain server-rendered HTML.
The title is under 72 characters and the claims match the diff, except that the PR is silent about the late test-title edit.
